audit.whatIsWrong: Disk chart gave Rumble levels 1 through 4-5, first item and two items, with only level 6 as 'Skill' — while every why on those rows says the opposite ('you own this all-in window', 'wins almost any level-3 all-in', 'out-trade his Flamespitter', 'this is your peak, close the lane here').
audit.why: The already-audited mirror states it directly: Rumble owns level 1 only, Kled leads from 2 through the first item, late is execution. The packet chart agrees and so does the 55.12% win rate.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 through 5 flipped to Kled and row 6 to Skill in both layers as one group; row 0 stays Rumble.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Equalizer is treated as a permanent threat with no cooldown given, and spikes[3] does not say what changes about it late.
audit.why: It is 130s at rank 1 but 80s at rank 3 — the reason the two-item stage flips is that his zone comes back nearly twice as often, not that it got stronger.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text now names the 80s at rank 3, and dontsFull[1].d gives the 130s rank-1 figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page says that Scrap Shield's move-speed burst can break the Bear Trap tether before it yanks.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction and the mirror already records it. Bear Trap only deals its bonus damage and pulls if the leash survives its duration — his W is a 6-second, always-available button that ends it. Every 'bait his shield' line on the page is really about this and never said so.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d rewritten to the tether break, and mid rewritten to bait the shield for that reason specifically.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (Q: bonus damage and yank only 'if shackled for a short duration')

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] describes 'E harpoon slow to kite you' and misses that Electro Harpoon carries two charges and shreds Magic Resist.
audit.why: The mirror records the actual sequence: both harpoons land before the Flamespitter cone, not after. That ordering is why the MR shred is up before the damage arrives, and it is why Mercury's Treads is the right boot here.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[0] rewritten to both harpoons first, MR shred, then Flamespitter.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (E: 'reducing their Magic Resist. Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time', range 850)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] told you to force the level 2-3 all-in without either cooldown that governs it.
audit.why: Bear Trap is 11s at rank 1 and Scrap Shield is a flat 6s — so the window is not 'when his shield is down', it is the few seconds after he spends it, and you get one trap per two shields.

edits.before: Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Its speed burst snaps the trap tether before the yank. Bait it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 — walk around the flame wall.

edits.before: Your Bear Trap (Q) percent-HP shred plus the re-E (E-W-E) burst owns the level 2-3 all-in before Rumble can stack Flamespitter heat — force it the second he steps to CS.

edits.after: His takeover: full-build Rumble overheats Flamespitter on your remount, and The Equalizer drops to 80s at rank 3 — every all-in costs your bar.

edits.after: Land both Electro Harpoons first to shred your MR, then burn Skaarl with Flamespitter

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay mine as long as I keep him in melee — my Bear Trap percent-HP damage and W on-hit shots out-trade his Flamespitter, and every time I remount I get a fresh health bar his single overheat window can't fully burn through. The thing to respect is his Equalizer (R): if he drops the flame zone across the choke he can zone my engage and deny the trade entirely, so don't all-in onto his R or I eat the whole channel. At 6 my own Chaaaaaaaaarge (R) lets me force a kill or knock him into terrain, and the speed trail extends ganks — bait his W shield and move speed out first, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay mine as long as I keep him in melee — my Bear Trap percent-HP damage and W on-hit shots out-trade his Flamespitter, and every time I remount I get a fresh health bar his single overheat window can't fully burn through. The thing to respect is The Equalizer (R): if he lays the flame wall across the choke he zones my engage and denies the trade entirely, so never all-in across it. At 6 my own Chaaaaaaaaarge (R) lets me force a kill or ram him into terrain, and the speed trail extends ganks — but bait Scrap Shield first, because that speed burst snaps my trap tether before it can yank him.

notes: Restated from the mirror rather than re-researched: the Scrap Shield tether break, the both-harpoons-before-the-cone ordering, and the Equalizer cooldowns. Following the mirror's warning, I asserted nothing about Scrap Shield creating terrain or displacing — those two derived flags contradict Riot's description, which is a shield plus a move-speed burst and nothing else. The packet suspectName 'Drop Equalizer' was a REAL error: the ability is 'The Equalizer', and it is corrected in wants.foe[2]. Packet reports games as 205 while the brief header says 378.
